description: The craft of designing games that people want to play: what makes a game, the mechanics-dynamics-aesthetics framework, core loops, level design, balancing and difficulty, narrative, playtesting and designing games that teach. Every idea is prototyped first on paper and then in the browser, played on a phone by classmates and revised from what the playtests show.
modelledOn: Schell, The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses
Fullerton, Game Design Workshop: A Playcentric Approach to Creating Innovative Games
Salen and Zimmerman, Rules of Play: Game Design Fundamentals
Koster, A Theory of Fun for Game Design
outcomes: Define what makes a game and analyse existing games in terms of goals, rules, feedback and player choice.
Apply the mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics framework to design and critique a core gameplay loop.
Design levels that teach, pace and challenge players, using flow, difficulty curves and spatial layout.
Balance a game's economy, progression and difficulty using spreadsheets, simulation and playtest data.
Write game narrative that works with play, drawing on local stories such as Ananse tales and Ghanaian history.
Plan and run playtests, interpret the results and iterate a prototype into a finished game for learning or entertainment.

units.title: What makes a game
topics: Definitions of play and games: goals, rules, conflict, outcome and voluntary participation; the magic circle
Formal elements: players, objectives, procedures, rules, resources, boundaries and outcomes
Types of fun and player motivation: Bartle's player types, self-determination theory, intrinsic and extrinsic reward
Traditional games as designed systems: oware, ludo, ampe and draughts analysed as rule sets
The designer's role and the iterative design cycle: idea, prototype, playtest, evaluate

units.title: Mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics
topics: The MDA framework: how designers and players see a game from opposite ends
Mechanics: actions, verbs, rules, space, objects and chance; emergent versus progression-based design
Dynamics: feedback loops (positive and negative), rubber-banding, snowballing and player interaction
Aesthetics: the eight kinds of fun (sensation, fantasy, narrative, challenge, fellowship, discovery, expression, submission)
Meaningful choice, uncertainty and risk; the role of randomness and skill
Deconstructing a popular mobile game with MDA

units.title: Core loops and prototyping
topics: Core loops, compulsion loops and session design; designing for short sessions on a phone
Paper prototyping with cards, dice and tokens; rapid digital prototyping in the browser
Game design documents, one-page designs and pitching a concept
Designing for constraints: touch input, small screens, intermittent data and low-end Android phones

units.title: Level design
topics: Goals of level design: teaching, testing, pacing and rewarding; the teach-test-twist pattern
Spatial design: sightlines, landmarks, chokepoints, guiding the player with light, colour and geometry
Flow theory and pacing: tension and release, interest curves and rest areas
Procedural versus handcrafted levels; seeds, constraints and quality control
Puzzle design: clear rules, aha moments, hint systems and avoiding guesswork
Building and critiquing a level set for a small puzzle or platform game

units.title: Balancing and difficulty
topics: Types of balance: symmetric and asymmetric, fairness, dominant strategies and transitive versus intransitive relations
Game economies: sources and sinks, inflation, resource flow diagrams (Machinations-style)
Difficulty curves, dynamic difficulty adjustment and accessibility options
Progression systems: experience, unlocks, skill trees and avoiding grind
Balancing with spreadsheets, cost curves and Monte Carlo simulation of play
Ethics of monetisation: loot boxes, dark patterns and fair free-to-play design

units.title: Narrative in games
topics: Story structure in games: linear, branching, emergent and environmental storytelling
Ludonarrative harmony and dissonance; letting mechanics carry meaning
Characters, dialogue systems and player agency; writing branching dialogue
Adapting oral tradition: Ananse stories, folktales and episodes of Ghanaian and African history as game narratives
Worldbuilding, tone and cultural authenticity; avoiding stereotypes

units.title: Playtesting
topics: Planning playtests: goals, recruiting players, scripts and the role of the silent observer
Methods: think-aloud, observation, questionnaires, interviews and gameplay telemetry
Usability and onboarding: first-time user experience, tutorials and teaching through play
Analysing results: separating symptoms from causes, prioritising changes, A/B tests
Running remote playtests on phones and collecting play data in the browser
Iterating a prototype across two playtest rounds and reporting the changes

units.title: Designing games for learning
topics: Serious games and gamification: what each is, and where points and badges help or hurt
Aligning mechanics with learning outcomes; intrinsic integration of content and play
Feedback, scaffolding and assessment inside the game; measuring whether learning happened
Case studies: games for literacy, mathematics, health and financial literacy (for example a susu savings game)
Designing for classrooms and community settings with shared or low-end devices
Project: a playable browser game for learning, such as a game about local history or an Ananse story, with a design document and playtest report

schedule.title: What games are and how they are designed
schedule.exercise: Choose a traditional game such as oware or ludo and write its rules as a formal-element table, then say which element you would change and what effect it would have.

tasks.title: Draw a diagram of ludo with its players, objectives, procedures, rules, resources, boundaries and outcomes, labelling each formal element
Work through a case study of oware, identify its resources and winning conditions, and decide what a rule change to capturing would do to play
Match four player profiles to a set of game features using Bartle types and self-determination theory, justifying the choice against given player feedback

schedule.title: MDA, mechanics and dynamics
schedule.exercise: Describe a game you know in terms of its mechanics, the dynamics they produce and the aesthetics a player feels.

tasks.title: Draw an MDA diagram for a card game, listing three mechanics, the dynamics that arise from them and the player experience on the other side
Diagram the feedback loops in a racing game with rubber-banding, marking each as positive or negative and predicting how a race ends
Diagnose a case-study game where the leader always wins by snowballing, choose a mechanic change, and justify it with the expected dynamics

schedule.title: Aesthetics, choice and deconstruction
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page MDA deconstruction of a mobile game you have played, citing specific mechanics for each type of fun.

tasks.title: Match eight scenario descriptions of play to the eight kinds of fun and justify each match
Assess five choices in a branching case study for meaningful choice, uncertainty and risk, and rate whether the choice matters to the outcome
Deconstruct a popular mobile game by diagramming its core loop, systems and rewards, and rank which mechanics drive retention

schedule.title: Prototyping and design documents
schedule.exercise: Make a paper prototype of a short dice game, run it with two friends and record three rule changes you made.

tasks.title: Draw the core loop of a quick mobile game for a 3-minute session, marking where the player is rewarded and where they decide to quit
Draw a one-page design as a labelled diagram, covering concept, audience, core loop, key mechanic and win and lose conditions
Evaluate a game concept against a low-end phone with a small screen and intermittent data, choose features to cut, and justify using the rubric

schedule.title: Level design and pacing
schedule.exercise: Sketch a level for a puzzle platformer that teaches one mechanic, tests it and adds a twist, annotating the player experience.

tasks.title: Lay out a three-room tutorial level that teaches, tests and twists a jump mechanic, with annotated player goals in each room
Draw a level map with sightlines, a landmark and a chokepoint, and mark the path you intend the player to follow and why
Plot an interest curve for a 10-minute level with tension peaks and rest areas, then place enemies and rewards to match the curve

schedule.title: Procedural levels and puzzles
schedule.exercise: Critique a set of five puzzle levels for difficulty progression, fairness and hint quality, and propose revisions.

tasks.title: Specify the constraints and seed inputs of a procedural level generator and diagram the checks that reject unplayable results
Judge four puzzle designs for clarity, aha moment and hint quality in a scored case study and choose the design to ship
Design a level set of eight puzzles that ramps difficulty, introducing each mechanic once, and document the intended solution of each

schedule.title: Balance and economies
schedule.exercise: Analyse the economy of a trading game, listing sources and sinks of coins and predicting whether inflation will occur.

tasks.title: Identify dominant strategies and intransitive relations in four balance scenarios and choose the fix for each with a justification
Draw a resource flow diagram with sources, sinks and converters for a farming game and mark where inflation can occur
Tune a difficulty curve and a dynamic difficulty rule for a case-study game so struggling players recover without making the game trivial

schedule.title: Progression, balancing tools and monetisation
schedule.exercise: Write a short ethics statement for a free-to-play game identifying three monetisation features you would refuse and why.

tasks.title: Design a skill tree with 12 nodes and unlock costs and diagram the intended progression order and the one choice that matters most
Model a card game's win rates in a spreadsheet-style table over 1000 simulated matches and adjust one cost until no card exceeds a 55 percent win rate
Review a free-to-play game case for loot boxes and dark patterns, score each feature against a fairness rubric and propose an ethical alternative

schedule.title: Story, characters and cultural narratives
schedule.exercise: Adapt an Ananse story into a game narrative outline with a core mechanic that carries the story's meaning.

tasks.title: Diagram a branching story with four endings, marking choice points and which endings are reachable from which decisions
Decide which of three mechanics fits a story about a trader's honesty and score each for ludonarrative harmony in a case study
Map an Ananse tale to quests, characters and a mechanic that expresses its trickster theme, in a story flow diagram

schedule.title: Playtest planning and onboarding
schedule.exercise: Write a playtest plan with goals, five tasks, a recruiting method and the observation notes template.

tasks.title: Choose goals, participants and a script for a playtest of a given prototype and score the plan against a rubric for bias and clarity
Select playtest methods for four design questions from think-aloud, questionnaires, interviews and telemetry, and defend each choice
Redesign a confusing first-time experience as a flow diagram that teaches three controls through play without a text tutorial

schedule.title: Analysing and iterating on playtests
schedule.exercise: Summarise two playtest rounds in a table of observations, causes, changes and results.

tasks.title: Sort 15 playtest observations into symptoms and causes, rank them by impact and choose the three changes to make first
Evaluate a remote playtest on phones with telemetry data in a scored scenario, choose the cause of drop-off at level 3, and recommend a change
Document a prototype's change between two playtest rounds in a before and after diagram of its flow and a table of what each change fixed

schedule.title: Serious games and learning outcomes
schedule.exercise: Write a learning-outcome map for a game teaching savings, linking each mechanic to an outcome and a measure.

tasks.title: Judge whether points and badges help in four gamification scenarios and justify each judgement against learner motivation
Map the learning outcomes of a fractions game to its mechanics and mark where content and play are intrinsically integrated or separate
Design in-game feedback, scaffolding and an assessment check for a literacy game and score it on whether learning could be measured

schedule.title: Learning game project
schedule.exercise: Write the project design document and playtest report outline for your learning game, with the audience, outcomes and test plan.

tasks.title: Analyse a susu savings game as a case study, identify what it teaches and where it fails to, and score it with the rubric
Adapt a game flow for a classroom with one shared device per group of six and plan turn-taking, roles and offline fallback
Produce the design diagrams for a browser game about local history: core loop, level or scene flow, learning outcomes and feedback points
